history.sg_progress: The Administration is continuing with its efforts to improve the budget formulation process. In order to refine the forecasting, the proposed budgets will reflect up-to-date financial performance data and the impact of foreseeable factors where possible, which should align with the mandate and operational tempo of the missions. The Administration agreed that the resource requirements can be carefully reviewed during budget formulation using a zero-based budgeting approach, bearing in mind the missions’ mandates and concept of operations and noting that the presentation in the reports of the Secretary-General will still reflect incremental changes related to staffing and financial resource requirements. In line with the recommendations of the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions and the requests of the General Assembly, detailed and comparative information, with justifications, will continue to be provided to facilitate the decision- making process. The Administration also notes that to enhance accuracy, predictability and transparency, the information in the budget reports will be enhanced by presenting holistic multi-year plans for construction and assets, as appropriate, including implementation status in the various budget periods. This is contingent upon the necessary system changes and available resourcing to implement the change within missions and support entities, and may require the prioritization of some multi-year elements, with financial value taking precedence.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration develop a strategy and propose to the General Assembly ways to improve budget development for peacekeeping operations, in order to achieve greater accuracy, predictability and efficiency.
history.administration_response: To improve budget development for peacekeeping operations, the Administration agreed that resource requirements could be carefully reviewed on a “zero-based” approach, where appropriate, bearing in mind the missions’ mandates and concept of operations. The recommendation of the Board will nevertheless not entail a change in the presentation of the reports of the Secretary- General, which will still reflect incremental changes related to staffing and financial resource requirements, to facilitate a detailed comparative analysis of budget proposals and related expenditure. It is envisioned that the Secretariat will move towards presenting multi-year budget estimates for construction, asset management and replacement plans in the context of the budget reports. This is contingent on the system changes and available resourcing necessary to implement the change within missions and support entities and may require the prioritization of some multi-year elements, with financial value taking precedence.
history.board_assessment: The 2025/26 budget, which is being prepared, would be the first to incorporate changes to reflect the first phase of this new approach. Under these conditions, an examination of the related budget documents (Secretariat budget report and supplementary packages), as well as the preparation process, will make it possible to measure the extent to which the recommendation has been implemented. The pending status is therefore considered in line with the principles governing the budget cycle.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration develop a strategy and propose to the General Assembly ways to improve budget development for peacekeeping operations, in order to achieve greater accuracy, predictability and efficiency.
history.administration_response: The Administration requests the closure of this recommendation because it was implemented. The changes were incorporated into the 2025/26 budget preparation process. This included enhancing the budget formulation process to allow missions to provide additional information and justification to support the review of their resource requirements on a zero-based budgeting basis. Budget proposals were reviewed to ensure that requirements were justified for the current budget period from a “zero base” and that all activities and expenditure contributed directly to the priorities and the mandate objective of the mission, not based solely on past budgets. Missions were also encouraged to propose and review resources from a multi-year perspective, where appropriate, in particular in the areas of construction, asset management and replacement plans. The supplementary information provided enhanced information on multi-year construction projects, facilitating a review of the initial plan and the actual expenditure during the project duration for each of the projects.
history.board_assessment: Given the progress made on the budget preparation process, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
